caption:
is my skin purging or breaking out?

"Purging" is the flare some people get in the first weeks of a product that speeds up skin turnover - retinoids most of all, and exfoliating acids like glycolic or salicylic. Spots that were already forming come up sooner. US prescribing information for tretinoin says it plainly: an apparent worsening of inflammatory acne may occur in the early weeks.

Three checks dermatologists commonly use:

The product. Does it contain a retinoid or an exfoliating acid? A plain moisturizer, cleanser or sunscreen has nothing in it to purge you. New spots after one of those are more likely a breakout or irritation from that product.

The place. Purging shows up where you usually break out. Spots in brand-new areas point somewhere else.

The clock. Purging usually settles within about 4-6 weeks. Still going past 8, spreading, burning or itching - that is worth showing a doctor.

What this does not mean: "purging" is a practical label, not a well-studied diagnosis. There is little formal research on it, and irritation can look similar. Use it to ask better questions, not to push through a reaction.
